senses.definition: (now rare) A strand of yarn etc. as used to guide one through a labyrinth; something which points the way, a guide.

quotes.text: she had even had in the past a small smug conviction that in the domestic labyrinth she always kept the clue.

senses.definition: Information which may lead one to a certain point or conclusion.
examples: Give me a clue because the question is too vague.

quotes.text: Black tracks on the magneto, a hairline crack in the flywheel casing, pitted points or a spitless exhaust — all are clues to potential conkouts

senses.definition: An object or a kind of indication which may be used as evidence.
examples: The detectives were looking for some clues at the scene of the crime.

senses.definition: Insight or understanding ("to have a clue [about]" or "to have clue". See have a clue, clue stick)
examples: I had little clue that I was being carefully monitored by the CCTV.

senses.definition: (crosswording) The text that indicates an answer in a crossword puzzle.

examples: The crossword compiler wasn't sure how to clue the word "should".

senses.definition: To provide someone with information which they lack (often used with "in" or "up").
examples: Smith, clue Jones in on what's been happening.

quotes.text: I stared into my mind for some image to clue me what to say but I saw only blackness there.
quotes.reference: 2014, John Macgregor, The Antibiography of Ian Mcnulty:

quotes.text: If the lee-side of the sail were clued up, the risk would be small compared with what it would be were the sheet nearly aft and the whole sail full of wind on starting the tack.
